claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets are governed by distinct local atomic structural environments.
Composition influences the formation of local atomic structural environments.
Processing conditions influence the formation of local atomic structural environments.
Rolling or forging can be used as the thermomechanical-processing intervention.
Adding or removing elements is the compositional intervention used to compare the quinary alloy with its subsets.
The proposed hypothesis applies at room temperature and at high temperature.
Relevant local structural environments include FCC structures, BCC structures, and grain-boundary structures.
Distinct local atomic structural environments cause variations in strength, ductility, and toughness.
Intersections between deformation paths can obstruct atomic sliding and dislocation motion, thereby changing flow-stress behavior.
The equiatomic quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy will have greater strength and toughness than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quinary alloy's predicted superior properties arise from a more stable and homogeneous local atomic structural environment.
The hypothesis may not generalize beyond the investigated compositions and processing conditions to other high-entropy alloys.
The exact relationship between local atomic structures and mechanical properties is not fully understood.
